usdRate.sourceName: World Bank WDI, official exchange rate (PA.NUS.FCRF), Niger
usdRate.note: 581.9 CFA francs per US dollar, 2025 average; the CFA franc is pegged at 655.957 per euro. The BCEAO transfer rates page showed 582.50 buying and 589.50 selling on 2 November 2026 (mid 586.0); its 30 October rates could no longer be read.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: BCEAO, monthly economic note for UMOA countries, September 2026 (harmonised consumer prices, August 2026)
inflation_cpi.note: Consumer prices fell 1.0% year on year in Niger in August 2026 after -2.0% in July (INS data via BCEAO); prices fell 4.5% on average in 2025 (World Bank) after a 9.1% jump in 2024.

inflation_projection.sourceName: BCEAO inflation target (1-3% band, centre 2%); Niger CPI averaged about 3.3% a year over 2021-2025 with large swings
inflation_projection.note: The CFA franc is pegged to the euro and the BCEAO targets 1-3%, but Niger's food-driven inflation swings widely (9.1% in 2024, -4.5% in 2025), so 2.5% is used for long-range plans.

policy_rate.sourceName: BCEAO, monthly economic note for UMOA countries, September 2026 (Monetary Policy Committee of 9 September 2026)
policy_rate.note: Main policy rate (refinancing rate) 3.00%, held on 9 September 2026; the marginal lending facility rate is 5.00%. Common to all eight UMOA countries.

savings_account_rate.note: No savings-account (livret) rate for Niger banks was found in BCEAO publications; banks declare term-deposit and contractual-savings rates only.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger), conditions créditrices
fdr_3m_rate.note: Median of the minimum term-deposit rates (taux DAT minimum) declared by 13 Niger banks, range 2.0-4.5%; the minimum usually applies to small, short deposits. Not a tenor-specific average.

fdr_1y_rate.note: The BCEAO publishes only each bank's minimum and maximum term-deposit rates (Niger medians 3.75% and 6.5%, first half 2026), not a 1-year rate.

dps_rate.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger), conditions créditrices (épargne contractuelle)
dps_rate.note: Median rate on contractual savings plans declared by 14 Niger banks for the first half of 2026; most declare 3.50% (range 2.7-5.0%).

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: No Niger-level average deposit rate was found: the BCEAO note gives only the UMOA average (5.15% in July 2026, Niger down 0.32 points in the month), and the World Bank's last Niger figure is 6.9% for 2016.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate sold to individuals was found; the Treasury borrows through UMOA-Titres auctions of 1-year bills and 2-5 year bonds, open to individuals through banks and licensed brokers (SGI).

tbill_91d_rate.note: Niger's Treasury issued only 12-month bills on the regional market in 2026 (last: 8.70% average yield on 1 October 2026); no 3-month bill rate exists.

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: UMOA-Titres, Niger Treasury auction of 1 October 2026 (bond maturing 3 July 2031)
tbond_5y_rate.note: Weighted average yield 8.62% on the 6.50% bond maturing 3 July 2031 (57 months); the 12-month bill in the same auction yielded 8.70%.

tbond_10y_rate.note: No Niger Treasury bond longer than 5 years was issued on the regional market in 2026 (UMOA-Titres Niger issue list).

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: Niger General Tax Code, article 80 (tax on income from claims, deposits and guarantees), eRegulations Niger
tax_bank_interest.note: 10% on interest from deposit and current accounts at banks (20% on other claims). The code version read is dated 2012 (older than 2025); later finance laws were not checked for changes to this rate.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate exists; the tax treatment of Treasury securities for individuals is set in each auction notice and was not confirmed.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: UMOA Council of Ministers, Decision of 30 June 2017 on FGDR-UMOA contribution rates and compensation ceilings (Article 2)
deposit_insurance_limit.note: Deposits are guaranteed up to 1,400,000 FCFA per depositor per bank (300,000 FCFA at a microfinance institution) by the regional deposit guarantee fund; decision from 2017 (older than 2025), still the one the fund publishes.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger), conditions débitrices (taux débiteur maximum)
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Median maximum lending rate declared by 13 Niger banks for the first half of 2026 (range 9-14%); it applies to all bank credit, including cards. No card-specific rate is published.

equity_return_low.sourceName: BCEAO, monthly economic note for UMOA countries, September 2026 (regional stock exchange BRVM, deposit rates)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: regional (BRVM) equities, where Niger investors buy shares, return about the bank deposit rate, as in their weak 2016-2020 years.

equity_return_base.sourceName: BCEAO, monthly economic note for UMOA countries, September 2026; BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger)
equity_return_base.note: Base case: about 1.5 points above after-tax large term deposits (median maximum 6.5% less 10% tax, about 5.9%), within the 4-point cap; the BRVM rose strongly in 2023-2026 but its 10-year record is uneven.

equity_return_high.sourceName: BCEAO, monthly economic note for UMOA countries, September 2026 (BRVM indices)
equity_return_high.note: High case: the BRVM repeats a strong decade like 2023-2026.

gold_return_low.sourceName: BCEAO exchange rates (CFA franc pegged to the euro)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: flat gold in euro terms.

gold_return_base.sourceName: BCEAO exchange rates (CFA franc pegged at 655.957 per euro)
gold_return_base.note: Base case: the long-run dollar gold trend of about 4% a year plus a small allowance for the euro-pegged franc weakening against the dollar.

gold_return_high.note: High case: strong gold years such as 2024-2025.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger), conditions créditrices
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: small term deposits or contractual savings at 3.5-3.75% less the 10% tax on bank interest.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger); UMOA-Titres, Niger Treasury auction of 1 October 2026
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: larger term deposits (median maximum 6.5%) less 10% tax, rounded down for the minimum amounts that the higher rates require.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: UMOA-Titres, Niger Treasury auction of 1 October 2026 (12-month bill 8.70%, 5-year bond 8.62%)
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: Niger Treasury bills and bonds at 8.6-8.7%, discounted for a possible tax and for payment delays after the 2024 sanctions period.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: No industry-wide life claim settlement ratio for Niger was found from CIMA or the Ministry of Finance.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Life insurers operate under the CIMA code, but no published term-life premium rates per 1,000 FCFA of cover by age were found from a public source.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay in Niger was found.

health_premium_table.note: No published private health insurance premiums by age per 100,000 FCFA of cover were found from a public source.

oop_health_share.sourceName: World Bank WDI, out-of-pocket expenditure (% of current health expenditure), Niger
oop_health_share.note: 51.5% in 2023 (WHO Global Health Expenditure Database); older than 2025, the latest available.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: BCEAO, monthly economic note for UMOA countries, September 2026; inflation assumption 2.5%
goal_inflation_health.note: No national medical CPI series was read; private medical costs usually rise faster than general prices, so 1.5 points above the 2.5% inflation assumption.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: BCEAO, monthly economic note for UMOA countries, September 2026; inflation assumption 2.5%
goal_inflation_education.note: No national education CPI series was read; private school fees usually rise faster than general prices, so 2 points above the 2.5% inflation assumption.

life_expectancy.sourceName: World Bank WDI, life expectancy at birth, total (SP.DYN.LE00.IN), Niger
life_expectancy.note: 61.4 years in 2024 (men 60.5, women 62.4); UN WPP 2024 gives 61.9 for 2026.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women (only the 65 total is published there).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: Working-age people per person aged 65+ = 100 / old-age dependency ratio: ratio 5.12 in 2025 (World Bank) gives 19.54; 5.2 in 2040 gives 19.23; 7.6 in 2065 (populationpyramid.net/niger/2065/) gives 13.16.

retirement_age_default.sourceName: WageIndicator, Niger social security (Decree 67-25 of 2 February 1967); CLEISS, Niger social security regime
retirement_age_default.note: Secondary sources: CNSS old-age pension at 60 for men and women with at least 180 months of contributions (CLEISS 2024), early at 55 for working women or workers unfit for work. No newer rule for people born after 1975 was found.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Le360 Afrique, 'Niger: l'âge de la retraite des fonctionnaires passe à 62 ans' (new general civil service statute)
retirement_age_government.note: The new general statute of the civil service raised the retirement age from 60 to 62 (May 2023, older than 2025); a January 2026 Council of Ministers decree extends 62 to auxiliary staff (APA, not read).

retirement_return_low.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger), conditions créditrices
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: small term deposits or contractual savings less the 10% tax on bank interest.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger), conditions créditrices
retirement_return_base.note: Base case: below after-tax large term deposits (about 5.9%) and the 1-year bill yield (8.7%), allowing for smaller balances and sovereign payment risk; not above the safe rate.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: UMOA-Titres, Niger Treasury auction of 1 October 2026
retirement_return_high.note: High case: part of the money in larger term deposits or Treasury bonds.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: BCEAO, banking conditions of UMOA credit institutions, first half 2026 (Niger)
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case: a mix earning about after-tax deposit rates.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: UMOA-Titres, Niger Treasury auction of 1 October 2026; equity base 7.5%; gold base 4.5%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: a balanced mix of deposits or Treasury bonds, regional equity funds and some gold.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: UMOA-Titres, Niger Treasury auction of 1 October 2026; equity high 12%

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: No non-contributory old-age pension for Niger was found; the CNSS 'allocation de vieillesse' is a contributory lump sum for insured people with 12-179 months of contributions (CLEISS).

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: No non-contributory old-age pension for Niger was found (CLEISS describes only contributory CNSS benefits).

gratuity_rule.sourceName: WageIndicator, Niger interprofessional collective agreement of 15 December 1972, article 34 (retirement indemnity)
gratuity_rule.note: On retirement the worker gets a retirement indemnity on the severance basis: average monthly pay of the last 12 months x 20% per year for years 1-5, 30% for years 6-10 and 35% beyond 10 (6, 9 and 10.5 days a year). Approximated as 6 days a year, 9.5 for all years once service exceeds 10, which matches the agreement at 30 years of service.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: CLEISS, Niger social security regime (CNSS old-age pension)
public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory CNSS pension for private employees from 60 after at least 180 months of contributions: since 2012, 20% of capped average pay plus 1.33% per year beyond 15 years, at least 60% of the minimum wage and at most 80% of pay; earnings capped at 500,000 FCFA a month. No indexation rule was found, so inflationLinked is false. Page dated 2024 (older than 2025).

fdr_3m.note: Banks declare minimum and maximum term-deposit rates to the BCEAO twice a year.

fdr_1y.note: Banks declare minimum and maximum term-deposit rates to the BCEAO twice a year.

dps.note: Monthly savings plans offered by banks.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate for individuals was found.

tbill_91d.note: Niger's Treasury issued only 12-month bills (bons assimilables du Trésor) on the regional market in 2026.

tbond_5y.note: Auctioned by UMOA-Titres in 2 to 5-year lines; individuals buy through banks or licensed brokers (SGI).

tbond_10y.note: No bond longer than 5 years was issued in 2026.

equity_fund.note: Supervised by the regional financial market authority (AMF-UMOA); funds invest on the regional exchange (BRVM).

gold.note: Niger produces gold; savers mainly buy it as jewellery.

centralBank.name: Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO)

insuranceRegulator.name: Commission Régionale de Contrôle des Assurances (CIMA)
insuranceRegulator.note: Regional insurance regulator for the CIMA member states; national supervision sits with the Ministry of Finance.

pensionScheme.name: Caisse Nationale de Sécurité Sociale (CNSS), old-age pension

depositInsurance.name: Fonds de Garantie des Dépôts et de Résolution dans l'UMOA (FGDR-UMOA)
